thanks for capturing this. I agree the warning reads unclear and appreciate your efforts to send a fix.
Happy to review your PR.

comments.author: ammar-iitm
comments.body:
Hi @karansgotit, thanks for the clear write-up and repro.

I dug into this and confirmed the root cause: in `_BaseEncoder._transform`, the `handle_unknown="infrequent_if_exist"` branch builds a single `columns_with_unknown` list and always emits the "will be encoded as the infrequent category" message for every column in it — but a column only actually falls back to the infrequent category if `self._infrequent_indices[i] is not None` for that column (see `_map_infrequent_categories`). A column with no infrequent category at all (e.g. no category was ever below `min_frequency`, or infrequent grouping isn't enabled) is instead encoded as all zeros, so the warning is wrong for that column.

I put together a fix that partitions `columns_with_unknown` into "has an infrequent category" vs. "doesn't", and emits a separate, accurate warning for each group:

```python
>>> import warnings
>>> from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder
>>> X = [["a", "x"], ["a", "x"], ["b", "x"], ["b", "y"]]
>>> ohe = OneHotEncoder(drop="first", sparse_output=False,
...                      handle_unknown="infrequent_if_exist", min_frequency=2).fit(X)
>>> with warnings.catch_warnings(record=True) as w:
...     warnings.simplefilter("always")
...     ohe.transform([["unknown_a", "unknown_b"]])
...     [str(x.message) for x in w]
["Found unknown categories in columns [1] during transform. These unknown categories will be encoded as the infrequent category.",
 "Found unknown categories in columns [0] during transform. These unknown categories will be encoded as all zeros."]
```

While fixing this I found the same inaccuracy also shows up when infrequent-category grouping isn't enabled at all (no `min_frequency`/`max_categories`, just `drop` set) — several existing tests (`test_ohe_handle_unknown_warn`, `test_ohe_drop_first_handle_unknown_ignore_warns`, `test_ohe_drop_if_binary_handle_unknown_ignore_warns`, `test_ohe_drop_first_explicit_categories`) asserted the old "infrequent category" wording even though the actual transform output was all zeros in those cases. I updated those to assert the correct "all zeros" message, and added a dedicated non-regression test for the mixed-column case from this issue.

Full diff, tests passing locally (`pytest sklearn/preprocessing/tests/test_encoders.py` — 266 passed, plus the OneHotEncoder common estimator checks):
https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/compare/main...ammar-iitm:scikit-learn:fix/ohe-unknown-warning-infrequent-vs-zeros

I saw @sundeep8967 also has a fix prepared — happy to defer / compare approaches, just sharing this in case it's useful. Let me know if a formal PR from this branch would be welcome.

title: Document tie-breaking behavior for max_categories in OneHotEncoder/OrdinalEncoder infrequent category grouping
body:
> [!WARNING]
> This issue is not yet ready for a PR. If you are interested in contributing to scikit-learn, please have a look at our [contributing guidelines](https://scikit-learn.org/dev/developers/contributing.html), and in particular the sections for [new contributors](https://scikit-learn.org/dev/developers/contributing.html#new-contributors) and the ["Needs triage"](https://scikit-learn.org/dev/developers/contributing.html#issues-tagged-needs-triage) label.

### Describe the issue linked to the documentation



When `max_categories` forces additional categories into the infrequent group beyond what `min_frequency` alone would select, and multiple categories are tied in count at the cutoff boundary, the docs for `max_categories` don't specify which tied category is kept as frequent vs. grouped as infrequent.

Looking at `_identify_infrequent()` in `sklearn/preprocessing/_encoders.py`, the tie-break is implicit rather than documented:

```python
# stable sort to preserve original count order
smallest_levels = np.argsort(category_count, kind="mergesort")[:-frequent_category_count]
infrequent_mask[smallest_levels] = True
```

Counts are sorted using `np.argsort(category_count, kind="mergesort")` — a stable sort — so ties are resolved by the order categories appear in `categories_[i]`, which for `categories='auto'` is lexicographic/numeric sort order. This behavior is not mentioned in the `max_categories` docstring or the User Guide section on infrequent categories (`encoder_infrequent_categories`).

### Suggest a potential alternative/fix

Add a sentence to the `max_categories` parameter docs (in both `OneHotEncoder` and `OrdinalEncoder`) and to the User Guide section on infrequent categories, stating that ties in category count are broken using the sort order of the categories (via a stable sort). This is also relevant to the discussion in #32161.

### Minimal reproducer

```python
import numpy as np
from sklearn.preprocessing import OneHotEncoder

X = np.array([["a"] * 2 + ["b"] * 2 + ["c"] * 5], dtype=object).T
enc = OneHotEncoder(max_categories=2, sparse_output=False).fit(X)
print(enc.infrequent_categories_)
# 'a' and 'b' tie at count=2 -- which one is grouped as infrequent
# is not documented, though it is deterministic.
```

### Additional context

Related: #32161 discusses tie-breaking by lexicographical order for encoder category ordering more broadly.

title: `propagate_callback_context` checks a public method but calls a private one
body:
> [!WARNING]
> This issue is not yet ready for a PR. If you are interested in contributing to scikit-learn, please have a look at our [contributing guidelines](https://scikit-learn.org/dev/developers/contributing.html), and in particular the sections for [new contributors](https://scikit-learn.org/dev/developers/contributing.html#new-contributors) and the ["Needs triage"](https://scikit-learn.org/dev/developers/contributing.html#issues-tagged-needs-triage) label.

In `sklearn/callback/_callback_context.py` the `CallbackContext.propagate_callback_context` method checks the public name while the call uses the private one (`_set_callbacks()`). This is the result of https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/pull/34096 which is where I think the private method was introduced.

```python
if callbacks_to_propagate and not hasattr(sub_estimator, "set_callbacks"):
    ...  # warn "does not support callbacks" and skip propagation

if callbacks_to_propagate:
    curr_callbacks = getattr(sub_estimator, "_skl_callbacks", [])
    # Now uses _set_callbacks
    sub_estimator._set_callbacks(curr_callbacks + callbacks_to_propagate)
```

Is it a requirement to support the private method as well if you want to implement an estimator with callback support? Or is the `if` statement a leftover from before?

I grepped for `set_callbacks` in `doc/developers/callback_support.rst` but couldn't find a mention of the private version
author: betatim

comments.author: betatim
comments.body:
A few more minutes of code reading lead me to realise that you have to inherit from `CallbackSupportMixin` (so say the docs), so I think this means for a third party estimator that wants to support callbacks this is also a requirement. If you inherit from it then you gain the private method "for free".

So I think I'll close this because the answer to my question is that I found this problem in the context of an estimator that doesn't inherit, which is "the bug".

it's imported in the cell before that
```py
import numpy as np

from sklearn.svm import LinearSVC


class NaivelyCalibratedLinearSVC(LinearSVC):
    """LinearSVC with `predict_proba` method that naively scales
    `decision_function` output."""

    def fit(self, X, y):
        super().fit(X, y)
        df = self.decision_function(X)
        self.df_min_ = df.min()
        self.df_max_ = df.max()

    def predict_proba(self, X):
        """Min-max scale output of `decision_function` to [0,1]."""
        df = self.decision_function(X)
        calibrated_df = (df - self.df_min_) / (self.df_max_ - self.df_min_)
        proba_pos_class = np.clip(calibrated_df, 0, 1)
        proba_neg_class = 1 - proba_pos_class
        proba = np.c_[proba_neg_class, proba_pos_class]
        return proba
```

title: Using `move_to` on a numpy array with negative stride crashes the Python process
body:
The `move_to` function we have for moving arrays from one namespace to another can crash the Python process when you ask it to move an array with negative strides. I found this while working on `PCA` where we have an array with negative stride (`Vt` from `_fit_truncated`).

The code below is a reproducer:

```python
import numpy as np
import torch
import sklearn
from sklearn.utils._array_api import get_namespace_and_device, move_to

def make_negative_strided():
    """A small, contiguous-source array viewed with a negative stride."""
    a = np.arange(12.0).reshape(3, 4)[:, ::-1]
    assert not a.flags["C_CONTIGUOUS"]
    assert a.strides[-1] < 0
    return a

a = make_negative_strided()
with sklearn.config_context(array_api_dispatch=True):
    xp, _, device = get_namespace_and_device(torch.asarray([1.0]))
    try:
        move_to(a, xp=xp, device=device)
    except Exception as exc:  # it is not caught
        print("Caught a Python exception (unexpected):", type(exc).__name__, exc)
    else:
        # this doesn't happen
        print("move_to returned without error (unexpected)")

    # instead the process exits with a SIGABRT
```

AI tells me that a possible fix is to call `np.ascontiguousarray(array)` if the input `array` is an array with negative stride. In addition we should [only apply this workaround in the case where the `move_to` target is torch](https://github.com/scikit-learn/scikit-learn/issues/34307#issuecomment-4778962780). The comment for the workaround should also include a link to https://github.com/pytorch/pytorch/issues/188023 and this issue so we can know when the work around can be removed.

Something like this, but with a check for torch as target:
```diff
--- a/sklearn/utils/_array_api.py
+++ b/sklearn/utils/_array_api.py
@@ def move_to(*arrays, xp, device):
             xp_array, _, device_array = get_namespace_and_device(array)
             if xp == xp_array and device == device_array:
                 converted_arrays.append(array)
             else:
+                strides = getattr(array, "strides", None)
+                if strides is not None and any(
+                    stride < 0 for stride in strides
+                ):
+                    # Some libraries (e.g. torch) do not raise a catchable
+                    # Python exception but abort the whole process when a NumPy
+                    # array with negative or zero strides is imported via DLPack
+                    # (such arrays are produced for instance by ``a[::-1]``
+                    # reversals, as done by ARPACK). The ``except`` clause below
+                    # therefore cannot protect against it, so the source array is
+                    # made contiguous first to guarantee positive strides.
+                    array = numpy.ascontiguousarray(array)
                 try:
                     # The dlpack protocol is the future proof and library agnostic
                     # method to transfer arrays across namespace and device boundaries
                     # hence this method is attempted first and going through NumPy is
                     # only used as fallback in case of failure.
                     # Note: copy=None is the default since array-api 2023.12. Namespace
                     # libraries should only trigger a copy automatically if needed.
                     array_converted = xp.from_dlpack(array, device=device)
```

What do others think about this? I am also wondering if this is a bug in numpy's DLPack implementation (should not expose arrays with negative stride) or if this is a bug in torch (should check for negative stride before doing anything)?

I think that `numpy.ascontiguousarray(array)` is free for most arrays, those that already full fill it. For arrays that are not already contiguous I don't know what the cost is, but I think there is no alternative?
author: betatim

comments.author: s23asd321-del

I can reproduce this and tested a small local fix.

My understanding is that the guard needs to happen before the DLPack path, because PyTorch can abort the process before Python can catch an exception. The fix I tested only materializes NumPy arrays with negative strides via `numpy.ascontiguousarray` before calling `xp.from_dlpack`; other arrays keep the existing path.

I also added a subprocess regression test so a failure cannot abort the pytest worker.

Would this be an acceptable direction? If yes, I can open a focused PR with the fix and test.
